items.english: Dusk had turned to evening, the silver lights shone full, and when the guests had at last scattered, there remained Tatsuya and Zenpei. With fresh dishes laid in a separate room, the two threw themselves into close talk. Setting down his cup to take breath, Zenpei said, "At this rate you will surely not refuse me. Though the fee for your good offices is small, let it stand at ten thousand yen, and upon success I will present a thousand yen yearly as thanks money. What, you say that to your colleagues and the others who have acted with you, the gentlemen here today, some share of allotment money is also due? That, well, indeed, such payments will have to be made, but in due course I shall consult on that point with my associates and arrange it in one way or another, so let the commission to yourself be fixed for now at just that sum, and first of all to bar the Kunitomo Company's application on its way and get my own before the ministry with all speed is the wise course, and in any case I would ask at once for your exertions toward bringing this matter together, leaving further reward to be settled once the affair is concluded, and I trust there will be no objection to that?"
notes: Zenpei's opening 'kore naraba, anata mo tokou wa gozarimasu mai' is deprecating and elliptical; I take it as pressing the offer while asking him not to refuse it as too small.

I kept 'ginshoku' as 'silver lights' rather than specifying candlesticks or lamps, and 'kan' / 'tsukasa' language as 'the ministry' to keep procedure concrete without importing a term the sentence does not name.
